findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant isolation for document reads
findings.body: When a user's tenant differs from the document's tenant, `canReadDocument` now returns `true` instead of rejecting access. Any caller relying on this exported authorization guard can therefore expose documents across tenant boundaries.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported document label contract
findings.body: Consumers of the exported `documentLabel` now receive `"Document record"` instead of `"Document"`. This is an observable contract change despite the PR's stated requirement to preserve existing contracts.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant equality enforcement
findings.body:
Every call now succeeds, allowing a user whose `userTenant` differs from `documentTenant` to read another tenant’s document. This removes the authorization boundary entirely.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported document label contract
findings.body:
Consumers or contract tests expecting the exported value `"Document"` now receive `"Document record"`. This is an observable API change despite the PR’s requirement to preserve existing contracts.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant isolation in the document-read authorization check
findings.body:
Any request where `userTenant !== documentTenant` now passes authorization, allowing cross-tenant document disclosure wherever this exported guard is used.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
